reviews.text:
We had our hot water heater go out.  We picked Intelligent because they had working hours on the weekends and didn’t charge extra for weekend hours.   Trevor came out to look at the issue with the hot water heater.   I personally thought it was the Thermopile, so I ran to hardware store replaced and issue still existed.   Trevor diagnosed it with a bad gas valve and said he can replace the heater part for $850 or he’d recommend a brand new water heater.  He said if he replaces the part, he will most likely need a brand new water heater anyway in the next few months to at least a year.   He then went on to look at the boiler, which was about 40 years old. Now keep in mind this boiler does work, and I was not planning to have any service on it whatsoever.  Over the years when I’ve had the maintenance guys over to look at the boiler all companies would not even touch it scared that they were going to break it even more and then have to owe me a brand new boiler.  He then went on to say he could give us a deal. We can kind of throw in a hot water heater. If you get a new boiler, we can install it this week.  So we thought about it a little bit more and we wanted to go ahead and do it because not only the savings but what if the boiler went out in the middle of winner then we’re going to pay extra charges for the winner cause they’re gonna be busy and it’s probably Probably gonna be more expensive.

So we went on to replace the boiler and the hot water heater hot water heater heater was replaced that day which was perfect. It took about an hour and a half.  He then said someone from Intelligent would call me to set up the install of the new boiler.  Two guys came out to install the new boiler and they brought another guy Neal who helped me I’ll walk through the process of what’s gonna happen and what they’re gonna install what they’re going to leave in place Place and not touched due to the fact that I made damage didn’t even more. Install took about 78 hours they did not have to come back the next day except to change out the thermostat just because that was kind of them. We had a small issue with the damper, but luckily they replaced that within the next day or two and now going on 24 hours to 48 without any issues.

Overall, I was very happy with their service very happy with their service service man. They were very polite and they explained what they were doing. They were in and out. They kept the place clean so I was very Happy with them overall.

reviews.author: Jeremy Gregory
reviews.text:
We had a sewer back up into the house at 10pm on October 29, 2025.  I called 3 plumbing companies and Rooter Hero responded within a 45 minutes.  Matt from Rooter Hero showed up and said they have an all day price of $79 for snaking a clean out.  This several hundred dollars cheaper than their competitors.  As he snaked the sewage line he hit a snag that choked up the snake, but was able to free up the blockage.  He said the snag was either a tree roots or broken pipe.  I decided to have them come back the next day with a camera check the line.   The price increased m to a little more than $300 with the clean cost included, but was still significantly lower than the clean out charge alone from their competitors.

The next day Matt returned with his project manager Braeden.  They ran a camera down the line.  First thing problem they noticed was the clean out.  It was recently replaced by Gilmore Heating, Air and Plumbing back in March of 2025, but inspected, not up to code.  Gilmore removed the original design and put in a 3” ABS “T”, they had told me the bull horn clean out wasn’t possible in that tight space.  Rooter Hero’s said that it must to be changed to bull horn clean out or it not California compliant and would fail inspection.  The second thing Rooter Hero’s camera revealed was a broken sewer line in the yard under the grass.  This also had be recently been replaced by Gilmore heating air and plumbing in March of 2025.  Rooter Hero’s camera showed a complete separation in the pipe.  At this time, I decided to move forward with Rooter Hero fixing both problems.  Braden wrote up the contract and they started the repair that same day.  Matt was present during entire project.  They were very thorough and communicated the whole process with me before they started and as they went through the process.  They had a team from Rooter Hero out in my yard fixing everything.

Matt, Francis and Evgenii dug out the pipes. They took pictures before and after and made sure these pictures were attached to the contract once completed. They found a coupler on a 45° angle that had separated and dropped about 1.5” from its connection.  Evgenii repaired all the lines.
The city came out in the morning of Tuesday, November 4th, 2025 to check the permitted work.  Passed without any problems.  Jesse and Marcelino back filled the yard hole yesterday.  Kon came today to back fill the driveway and fill it with concrete.  Everything looks great.  All these guys were professional and did an outstanding job.  I appreciate Rooter Hero’s dedication to immediately correcting work previously done by a non reputable plumbing company.  Then completely walking me through the process.  I feel their customer is commendable and should be recognized.  I am beyond grateful to this team of plumbing professionals.  I highly recommend them.

reviews.author: kao xiong
reviews.text:
TLDR:
Got service for caulking bathtub.
Bad job and would not refix.
Issued refund but took a LONG time to receive.
End of day, TERRRIBLE communication from PGA.

My parent's got service at their home for a few things.
This was all done and paid for on 09/15/2025.
Everything was done fine with exception of caulking around the bathtub.

1) The caulking was not done well
2) There was no communication as to not use the the bathtub for a given period of time

I reached out to PGA and spoke with the scheduler.
He told me any disputes would have to go thru his boss, Rob.
He forwarded me to Rob's number, and I left a message.
This was on 09/16/2025.

I did not hear anything back so I reached back out on 09/24/2025 and left another message for Rob.
Rob called me back on Thursday, 09/25/2025, and I explained to him what the situation was.
I sent him pictures of the poor service and he said he would have to look into it and will let me know.

Monday, 09/29/2025, still nothing from Rob, so I texted him.
They responded and said Rob is out of the office this week at a conference in Colorado and will be back next Monday.
I responded with a bit of frustration as I talked to Rob on Thursday and he NEVER mentioned that he was going to be gone for a week.
I would think if he was going to be gone he would wrap up my situtation or pass it along to someone else in the organization.
But we were patient, we gave them the week.

Monday, 10/06/2025, still no call back or communication from Rob.
I reached back out to get a status update.
He finally respondeds saying he wasn't pleased with the appearance (from the pictures we provided) and that he can schedule another visit to correct the problem.
I told him that we would not expect to be billed again since we already paid for this service.
He said since we ran the shower too soon (reminder, the service tech never gave my parents any communication that they should wait any ceratin period before usage) he'd stil have to charge us labor.
I responseded if he cannot fix it free of charge, to refund our money and we'd take our business elsewhere.

No response for Rob.
Wednesday, 10/08/2025, I reached back out to him.
He responded that they could not redo the service free of charge and that he will issue a refund for $131.88 thru a check thru mail.
I said, ok, we'll look for the refund in the mail.

Wednesday, 10/22/2025, we've still have not received the refund so I reach back out.  We are pretty frustrated at this point.

No response again, so I reach out again on Thursday, 10/23/2025 and got a hold of someone.
This person told me, since Rob supposed issued the refund, any resolution has to go thru Rob.
And Rob is currently out all day in meetings and a message has been relayed to him.
I expressed my frustation saying, is there no other person that can help.  We've waited patiently already close to a MONTH.
All this person could offer was an apology.

Finally Friday, 10/24/2025, Rob responds and says check is in the mail.
Not apology, nothing.
I respond expressing more frustrations also saying I will leaving a bad review for them.
Ofcourse he responds quickly now when he hears he is going to get a bad reivew.

Thursday, 10/20/2025, my dad finally receives the refund check in the mail.

So yes, PGA does do good work.  But when it is not good work, good luck working with Rob on getting it resolved.
DO NOT expect any kind of reasonable customer service, communication from Rob.

Attached are the pictures of the serivce that was provided and my communication thread with Rob.

reviews.author: Randy Leach
reviews.text:
READING THIS REVIEW MAY SAVE YOU A LOT OF MONEY AND FRUSTRATION!!

It’s a bit lengthy but worth the read…

I had Powell’s Plumbing & Air stop by to give me a quote to replace my water heater (I purchased a new Rheem ahead of time)…redo/clean-up the “octopus” of water lines in the closet where the water heater is located, and remove my water softener from the adjacent closet. I made sure I conveyed to him that I wanted ALL new copper piping. The quote was $1764.

The next day I decided to just have the water softener disconnected so I can see how the water will be without it before getting rid of it. I am having the flooring redone, so at least I can move the softener out, then back in. I stopped by their office and spoke with the office staff and they agreed and reduced my quote to $1471.

The day of replacement…this is when it gets interesting.

Powell’s Plumbing and Air arrived. I went over the work with the plumber. He stated that I can just turn the built-in valve behind the water softener and that will bypass it, which he did. He then unplugged the power adaptor and literally just threw it down on the floor. Ok…not what I was expecting, but this was a sign of things to come.

I touched base with him again about all the new work being done in copper. He replaced the water heater and used copper pipe for the water lines, but when he went to connect the pipe for the Pressure Relief Valve, he brought in a dirty piece of PEX tubing that looked like it was salvaged from another job.

I asked him why was he using that when I had specifically requested ALL copper. He stated he didn’t have any more copper pipe. After having to press the issue, he turned to head to out to his truck and said “Pain in the Ass.” I was taken aback. The plumber also had an HVAC guy with him who was just “shadowing” him, not doing any of the work. The HVAC guy actually apologized for the plumber’s behavior and comment.

Upon the plumber’s return, low and behold he had a piece of copper pipe. It must have magically appeared on his truck. So, not only did he say “Pain in the Ass” but he also looked me right in the face and straight out lied.

The octopus of water lines was never fixed (see attached picture). He just said “We’ll get it next time.” Next Time??? I’m paying to have this done now!! At this point I was fed up with his behavior and just wanted him gone.

So, I was cussed…lied to…and all the work wasn’t performed. There was ZERO CORRECTION in pricing. I paid for EVERYTHING to be done and ended up with just a straight forward water heater replacement. Oh, and it was easy access…ground floor, zero steps, drain right beside it, and about 25 feet to the front door.

Powell’s Plumbing & Air supplied about 10’ of copper pipe, a few fittings, a shutoff valve, and the expansion tank. I estimate those materials would probably take up the better portion of the $171 of the $1471. So, the hour and a half labor ended up costing me $1300. That’s $866 an hour!! My doctor doesn’t even charge that much…let that sink in a bit!!

reviews.author: Terri Mcgaughey
reviews.text: From the first call I made on, it has been nothing but a pleasant experience. I don’t know much about this company as it my first experience with them, but I can say that they sent out one of their best representatives/technicians when they sent Colin French. At age 68, I can tell a man with good character when I see one, which is rare these days. He was polite and extremely respectful of my home and especially to myself. He explained everything that needed done to fix my water pressure problem in a way that I could easily understand. He also provided me with updates as the work was being done. He installed new plumbing throughout and re-routed it away from my electric panel, new pressure tank, gauges and valves in my almost 100 year old log cabin. Prior to his great job, I had practically zero water pressure and it would take at least 2 hours to fill up the bathtub and my washer couldn’t even detect H2O, so I couldn’t use it at all. I had 3 other companies come to my home prior to Apex. None of the other 3 impressed me at all. However, Apex (Colin) did from the get-go. I consider Colin a remarkable representative for the Apex company. He brought with him an apprentice (Mo). He was a fine representative of the company as well. I was within ear shot and was impressed with Colin’s teaching ability. The cost was fair considering the amount of work that was done and the professional, yet personal service that I received. To be honest, they came in as Plumbers, but left as what I consider friends, even if our paths never cross again. Based on my experience, I highly recommend Apex. Ask for Colin, you won’t be disappointed.

I have been a customer of Emerald Plumbing for many years and have been consistently impressed with their professionalism- from the initial phone call to the completion of the project. My most recent experience was no different.

I called Emerald last Friday in reference to my garbage disposal not working. I was scheduled for today (Monday). The technician, Mike called to let me know he was en route. Mike arrived promptly and diagnostic the unit. As it was leaking, he determined that it was rusted out and needed to be replaced. Mike had an identical garbage disposal on his truck and quickly replaced the old one. Mike was friendly, courteous, and professional the whole time he was here. All of the work was completed in short order and for a very reasonable price. My experience with Mike was typical of what I have experienced with Emerald Plumbing over the years as their technicians are always professional, courteous, and do excellent work.

I highly recommend Emerald Plumbing.

reviews.author: Luther F. Davis III
reviews.text:
A residential re-piping project can be a daunting undertaking for many homeowners, but from the first phone call to the final follow-up, Emerald Plumbing truly put the customer first. Darren, the project consultant and estimator, was polite, knowledgeable, and customer-oriented. Despite minimal lead time, Emerald was able to begin the project just two days after we made our final decision to move forward.

Myrna in the office was friendly and professional, coordinating all appointments for the re-pipe as well as the follow-up drywall repair. Onsite project manager Chad did an excellent job explaining the work beforehand and thoroughly reviewing everything once the job was complete. His crew was clean, organized, and respectful of our home, using drop cloths in all traffic areas. They worked quickly and efficiently without sacrificing quality.

The subcontracted drywall repair exceeded our expectations, leaving the walls textured and paint-ready, far better than we had anticipated. Vice President Hugo even followed up personally to ensure our satisfaction.

The entire team was friendly and professional, and my wife and I have nothing but great things to say. Our home has been significantly upgraded, and what could have been a stressful, daunting project turned out to be a smooth and positive experience. Thank you again to the entire team at Emerald Plumbing.

reviews.author: Sir Ronan
reviews.text: Hugo / Chad / the rest of the crew are professional / polite / thorough / etc. I can't say I have a single negative thing to say about them. I am happy with the entire process. The 3rd party drywall repair company same, no complaints. As someone who dealt w/ a myriad of CPVC issues, yes re-pipes are inherently expensive, but you're getting quality work & if you have CPVC that is 10+ years old, do not wait until it ruins your day, re-pipe as soon as you can! Thx again to Emerald for their quality work. & shout out to the office staff, they were lovely as well!

reviews.author: W Z
reviews.text:
This company seems much more focused on making money than meeting customer needs. I contacted them to have a licensed plumber check the gas connections for my water heater and HVAC, just to confirm there were no leaks. I didn’t suspect a leak, but wanted professional verification.

When scheduling the appointment, I clearly explained my request. However, they refused to provide a quote for the gas leak check. Instead, they said there would be a minimum $99 fee, and that the actual cost couldn’t be determined until the technician assessed the situation onsite. OK, fine.

When the plumber arrived, I again explained that I was looking for a simple gas leak check and verification. After a quick 10-minute look at the appliances, he told me the only test he can offer is a pressure test — priced at $1,000. I was shocked. There are many standard, less expensive methods for detecting gas leaks (e.g., visual inspection, soapy water test, electronic gas detectors, gas sniffers), yet they only offered the most expensive option.

I asked how long the pressure test would take and was told less than an hour. So essentially, I paid $99 just to get a quote for a $1,000 test that involves no repairs — just using their tools and a plumber's time for an hour. That’s effectively $1,000/hour.

Later, I contacted another plumbing company. Their pricing was less than half of Benjamin Franklin’s, and their service included more comprehensive checks and other items.

Given this horrible experience, I will not be using Benjamin Franklin Plumbing again.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[Comment after reading “Response from the owner”]

The owner’s response only reinforces my original impression — that this company prioritizes making money over addressing customer needs. They seem to exaggerate every situation to justify selling more expensive services.

In my case, I simply wanted a basic gas leak check and verification, with no known issues or suspected leaks. Yet, they offered only one option — a $1,000 pressure test — while dismissing other standard and legitimate methods used across the industry. Their reasoning was, “$1000 would be a small price to pay if it prevented a fire or worse yet the loss of someone’s life.”

If that logic applies to everything, then perhaps they should set a $1,000 minimum for all services. For example, if a customer only needs to install a gas shutoff valve, they could insist on a $1,000 pressure test, because, “$1000 would be a small price to pay if it prevented a fire or worse yet the loss of someone’s life." Or if someone wants to install a water shutoff valve, they might recommend a $1,000 water pressure test — since, by their reasoning, “it could prevent water damage that costs tens of thousands to repair.”

This kind of approach doesn’t demonstrate care for customer safety — it shows a business model focused on upselling and inflating costs under the guise of safety.
